lesson_title: Mastery check: using a mouse and trackpad
essential_question: How can understanding computers around us help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: This is day 5 of "Computers Around Us". That is unit 2 in grade 3. Today is a mastery demonstration about using a mouse and trackpad. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Label a diagram of computer parts and demonstrate three careful-use habits. Today helps by working on using a mouse and trackpad. Your unit also covers parts of a computer, input and output devices, caring for devices, and software versus hardware. Today counts for a grade. Do it on your own.
primary_task: Show that you can do this on your own: using a mouse and trackpad. Put away the help sheet and the examples. Solve a new problem all the way. First write what answer you expect. Then test it two ways. Include one tricky case. Show what you expected and what you got. Then explain your thinking. Write it so someone new to using a mouse and trackpad could follow it. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about using a mouse and trackpad. It is part of "Computers Around Us". Later days in this unit cover other things, like parts of a computer. Before you stop, do this check: Rate confidence in using a mouse and trackpad, cite one piece of evidence from today, and choose: ready to extend, ready to review later, or need a different explanation. In grade 3 you need one clear try with a grown-up nearby. Say or write your reason in a sentence or two. Drawings, objects, or spoken answers are all fine.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task names a hand or body skill (using a mouse and trackpad) as the thing being learned. If that is hard for you, you may use a different way instead — one hand, a switch, voice typing, a bigger or different mouse, eye control, or an adult typing while you say the answer. Using a different way is worth full marks.
You can do this with the keyboard only, no mouse needed. Text can be made bigger, and you may do it on paper instead of a screen.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never require a real password, private message, precise location, account credential, API key, or identifiable image.
Use only fictional or sandboxed systems, accounts, and data; never probe, exploit, or attempt to access a real external system.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify, not as an authority or a substitute for learner work.
The tutor may explain, demonstrate, or debug alongside the learner, but must not silently complete a graded project or assessment for them.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting using a mouse and trackpad.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for using a mouse and trackpad follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for using a mouse and trackpad, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for using a mouse and trackpad works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of using a mouse and trackpad, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking using a mouse and trackpad mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply using a mouse and trackpad under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on using a mouse and trackpad rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
